item.text:
Finding 2 now has the same treatment as finding 1: a candidate fix, implemented in the diagnostic copy and validated.

**The fix and its validation.** In `work/diag/omnipaxos_runtime/src/actor.rs`, `push_to_sub` and `push_to_all_subs` now set the subscriber cursor to the position the read ended at after a complete read, instead of counting delivered items (the two edits are marked `DIAG-ONLY CANDIDATE FIX for finding 2`, alongside the earlier finding-1 change — `diff` against the captured source shows both).

| build | finding-2 repros | finding-1 repros | captured `async_runtime_test` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| captured source | 0 passed / 2 failed | 2 passed / 6 failed | 24 passed |
| diagnostic copy, both fixes | **2 passed / 0 failed** | **8 passed / 0 failed** | **24 passed / 0 failed** |

The subscriber streams become what the docs promise: fully compacted → `[Snapshotted(6)]` once (was six repeats); partially compacted → `[Snapshotted(3), Decided(103), Decided(104), Decided(105)]`, each delivered exactly once (was 104/105 twice). So finding 2's root cause is confirmed by construction as well as by symptom, the two fixes coexist, and neither disturbs the captured expectations.

**Also this turn:** the captured runtime suite proved stable under load — 8 consecutive runs with 12 CPU hogs on 4 cores, 24/24 every time — a useful contrast with finding 3's captured-test symptom and evidence that finding 1's race is not leaking into the captured shapes.

[`repro.sh`](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-16_23-10-28-omnipaxos-baseline/work/repro.sh) now covers both fix checks; I re-ran it end-to-end and the report's printed output matches:
